Annual unmet hours per upgraded dwelling unit Figure 9 shows the annual energy consumption savings from individual and combined envelope measures, based on 27.8% of dwelling units where all three individual measures apply. When all measures are implemented together, 91.1% of the units experience total savings that are slightly lower than the sum of the individual savings, while 8.9% see total savings that slightly exceed the sum of the individual impacts. The slightly lower savings observed in most units result from overlapping effects among the measures. For example, both attic insulation and advanced air sealing reduce heat loss, but their impacts partially overlap, so the combined effect is not fully additive. For the 8.9% of dwelling units that achieve higher savings from the envelope package, the benefit comes from the HVAC performance curve, particularly for cooling. The envelope package yields greater improvements in cooling energy consumption per unit of delivered cooling than the sum of the individual measures. Although it reduces delivered cooling less than the sum of the individual measures, the efficiency gains result in higher overall energy savings. 14 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. Figure 10 shows the aggregated average daily baseline energy consumption in Colorado, with February 20 identified as the day with the highest energy use.
